audience.notes: Australian couples in their 30s, AUD 150K plus, many comparing a home venue with one abroad (Italy, Bali, Dubai, Fiji). Time-poor professionals who like a clean sheet but have never vetted a venue overseas. The paying parent reads for money and legal certainty. Do not write for the price-only reader: no 'cheapest venue' framing, no discount talk; price is one weighted column, not the decision.

payload.search_intent: Mixed: transactional-informational. Readers want a template they can copy now, then help deciding what goes in it and how to choose between rows. SERP is template sellers and aggregators with almost no guidance.
payload.angle: The free venue shortlist tab, ready to copy, with the destination columns nobody else includes, a weighting method that turns the sheet into a ranked decision, and the invisible checks a Wedded Advisor runs before a venue earns a row.
serp_gaps_to_win: A free, copyable table on the page itself (competitors are paid Etsy files, Scribd PDFs or Pinterest pins).
A clear weighting and scoring method (no ranking page explains one).
Columns for venues abroad: legal ceremony on site, transfers and access, room blocks, quote currency, local curfew and noise, wet-weather plan.
AUD and Australian framing (minimum spend, venue hire, service charges) instead of US 'rental, tax, gratuity'.
An expert, up-to-date guide; the only editorial result (Wedinspire) is from 2023.

outline.h2: The venue comparison spreadsheet to copy
outline.answers: What columns should my venue comparison spreadsheet have, and can I just copy one?
must_include: Open with a 2 to 3 sentence answer: one row per venue, the 16 columns below, fill it during or straight after each enquiry or tour.

A Markdown table readers can paste into Google Sheets or Excel, header row plus 2 blank example rows, columns in this order: Venue, Location, Capacity (seated and standing), Exclusive use, Date availability, Minimum spend or hire fee, Inclusions, Catering, Accommodation, Ceremony space, Wet-weather plan, Curfew and noise, Access and transfers, Deposit and cancellation, Legal ceremony on site (abroad), Notes.
Tip from the AI Overview consensus, in our words: write 'included' rather than leaving a cost blank, and leave a cell empty only when you have not asked yet, so gaps show at a glance.
Soft line: the same shortlist can live in Wonderland Studio (link /wonderland-studio).

outline.h2: What each column is really asking
outline.answers: What do I write in each column, and what is the catch behind it?
must_include: One or two lines per column grouped as Space and date, Money, Food and stay, Rules and risk.

Money: minimum spend versus hire fee, what counts towards the minimum, service charges, and the currency the quote is in. No dollar figures unless researcher sources them; link /expert-advice/average-venue-cost-for-wedding for typical costs instead of repeating its numbers.
Exclusive use: whether other events share the grounds, the pool or the restaurant that day.
Deposit and cancellation: when deposits fall due and what is refundable; mention Australian consumer rights only via the researcher with an official source.
Link /expert-advice/wedding-expenses-spreadsheet for tracking deposits once booked.

outline.h2: How to weight the columns and score your shortlist
outline.answers: How do I turn the sheet into a decision when every venue wins on something?
must_include: Three steps: mark 3 non-negotiables as pass or fail (e.g. date, capacity, legal ceremony on site); weight the rest 1 to 3; score each venue 1 to 5 per column and multiply.
A tiny worked example with 2 or 3 invented, unnamed venues (Venue A, B, C) and no prices, showing a beautiful venue losing on transfers and wet weather.
A simple formula readers can paste (SUMPRODUCT of scores by weights), written in plain words too.
Warn against weighting price so heavily that it decides alone (subtle anti-bargain-hunter framing, never preachy).

outline.h2: Questions to ask before a venue earns a row
outline.answers: What do I need to ask a venue so I can fill the sheet honestly?
must_include: Short: 6 to 8 questions mapped to the columns, not a long list.
Must link /20-essential-questions-to-ask-your-wedding-venue-before-booking with a non-exact anchor (e.g. 'our full list of venue tour questions'); never the anchor 'questions to ask wedding venue'.
Include who answers: response time and whether one named coordinator owns your wedding (planning-from-afar fear).

outline.h2: What changes when the venue is abroad
outline.answers: Which columns matter more, or only exist, when we compare a venue overseas?
must_include: This is the invisible-work section. Cover: legal ceremony on site versus a symbolic ceremony after a registry wedding; transfers and access for older guests (stairs, boats, cobblestones, distance from the airport); room blocks and minimum nights; quote currency and payment schedule; local curfew and amplified music limits; wet-weather plan with a real indoor space for full guest count; time zones and reply speed.
Link /expert-advice/weddings-abroad-where-can-you-legally-get-married for legal basics; no country-specific legal claims without researcher sources.
Link /tips-for-booking-a-wedding-venue-abroad and /destination-weddings/hidden-costs-destination-wedding.

Show what a Wedded Advisor checks before a venue reaches a couple's sheet (site knowledge, contracts, payments across currencies, transfers), using only claims supported by brand-profile.md or /wonderland-concierge.

outline.h2: Where to find venues worth comparing
outline.answers: Where do I find a shortlist to put in the spreadsheet?
must_include: Strong link to the Marketplace venue search /search?tab=venues (78 venues, filters by location, capacity and venue type, verified 24 Nov 2026). Describe the filters plainly.
Link /search?tab=vendors once, for planners and caterers that sit alongside the venue (category chips, regions servicing, languages).
Link /venue (venues by city), /au/venues-in-sydney, /ae/venues-in-dubai, and destination pages /destinations/europe/italy and /destinations/asia/bali.
Do not link /marketplace (NOT LIVE in link map). Do not name individual /venue/<slug> profiles as recommendations unless the team confirms.

outline.h2: When to hand your shortlist to a Wedded Advisor
outline.answers: At what point is the spreadsheet not enough?
must_include: Signs: more than one country on the sheet, cells you cannot fill from Australia, quotes in different currencies, older guests with access needs.
What the advisor does with the sheet: checks the columns couples cannot verify from home, compares contracts, and keeps deposits and currency in one place (only claims from /wonderland-concierge).
Link /wonderland-concierge. Low-pressure tone; the spreadsheet remains useful either way.

faq.q: What should a wedding venue comparison spreadsheet include?
faq.a_note: List the 16 columns in one sentence; point to the table.

faq.q: How many venues should we compare?
faq.a_note: Practical shortlist guidance (e.g. 3 to 5 toured or video-walked) framed as advice, not a statistic.

faq.q: Is there a free wedding venue comparison template?
faq.a_note: Yes, the table above copies into Google Sheets or Excel; Wonderland Studio keeps it with the budget and guest list.

faq.q: How do you compare a venue in Australia with one overseas?
faq.a_note: Same sheet, add the abroad columns, convert quotes to AUD on one date and note the rate.

faq.q: Should price be the most important column?
faq.a_note: Weighted, not decisive; total cost at your guest count matters more than the headline fee.

must_include: Couple fear 1 (hiring the wrong planner, someone polished but unreliable): a 'who answers and how fast' check, and the advisor section explaining vetting of who is on the ground.
Couple fear 2 (planning from the other side of the world): columns and questions that can be filled from Sydney, video walkthroughs, reply times, time zones.
Paying parent fears: hidden costs and currency (minimum spend, service charges, quote currency) and legal validity (legal ceremony on site column).
A copyable table with exactly the 16 columns listed in H2 1.
A weighting method with a worked example.
Wet weather, transfers, legal, room blocks and budget all appear as invisible work.
5 FAQs.
Australian English and AUD framing.
must_avoid: Colons in H2s or headings; em dashes anywhere.
Exact-match anchor 'questions to ask wedding venue' (owned by /20-essential-questions-to-ask-your-wedding-venue-before-booking).
Repeating cost figures from /expert-advice/average-venue-cost-for-wedding; invented prices or statistics.
Any Wedded World plug or link (/wedded-world, /wedded-world/melbourne).
Links to /marketplace, DRAFT URLs from link-map, or anything in 'Do not link from blogs'.
Copying text or table layouts from Etsy, Scribd, WordLayouts or other ranking templates.
Recommending specific venues or naming venue profiles as partners without team confirmation.
Country-specific legal rules without a researcher-sourced official link.
Cheapest-venue or discount framing aimed at the bargain hunter.
